title: Who really owns Room 404?
situation: Two guests swear they booked Room 404 at the same moment, and the hotel has only one key.

goals.Pierce: Keep both guests happy without anyone blaming him for the double booking.
goals.Vex: Get through one night without answering another impossible question.
goals.Madame Halloran: Restore order and make the hotel look respectable in front of the guests.
goals.Sir Hallucinate: Prove he booked Room 404 first, using facts he is certain are true.
goals.Captain Timeout: Get the room he booked and finish one full sentence for once.

secrets.Pierce: He booked Room 404 himself, under a fake name, because he wanted one quiet night to rest.

beats.speaker: Pierce
beats.intent: Pierce runs into the lobby shouting that two guests want Room 404 and the only key is humming at him. |

beats.speaker: Sir Hallucinate
beats.intent: He announces that he booked Room 404 at noon, that the room was built for him in 1787, and that everyone knows this.

beats.speaker: Captain Timeout
beats.intent: He arrives claiming the same booking, starts his sentence, cuts out mid-word, and restarts from the beginning again and again.

beats.speaker: Vex
beats.intent: Vex checks the booking ledger and finds both bookings under the same name: Pierce.

beats.speaker: Madame Halloran
beats.intent: She demands order, and the lamp's missing cord hums back through the keyhole of Room 404 as everyone argues. |

beats.speaker: Sir Hallucinate
beats.intent: He insists the ledger is wrong, that Captain Timeout is actually a teapot, and that Vex invented the name Pierce.

beats.speaker: Captain Timeout

beats.speaker: Pierce

beats.speaker: Madame Halloran

beats.speaker: Pierce
beats.intent: Pierce opens Room 404 to find both guests asleep in it, each in half a room split by tape, and the humming key finally quiets as he says: Welcome! Sorry. Welcome again.
